Start from 81239c3e, whose production code is the qualified c942b254 checkpoint. Full default compile mean 9658.3887 ns, absolute 95% mean interval [9616.7066,9698.8797]; 7000 ns target remains unmet. Reference source d4b5eb56bf24654e510231f1d1251f592cefa185519376dff47190ac3d20649c, native 6a47ef4a9a66b15245bc18bb4ee6c3a457434ab80d9cd42effc62506319e32b3.

Hypothesis: immutable line geometry can precompute a conservative axis-aligned enclosure of every point that passes the actual rounded position predicate. A point outside that enclosure can skip the original predicate cheaply, preserving its original ordered query even after collisions move the point. This differs from the rejected per-point miss-region cache: certification happens once at line construction, with no per-sweep certificate building, persistent miss state or change to required history snapshots.

First stage is an untimed shadow diagnostic in a private source snapshot. Keep the original kernel and verify every predicted rejection against its actual result; count visits, eligible visits and exclusions. No production skip or speed claim yet. Test finite/extreme/subnormal/degenerate/flipped/extended geometry and boundary points, then independent replay and exact default track/work. If promising, predeclare fixed 12 direct compiler pairs and require KEEP with upper95 time delta <= -5% to justify the additional numerical machinery. Full confirmation, broad/default/large guards, memory, isolated stepping and structural parity still required for adoption. No runtime/build flags, quality or denominator changes.

Proof outline for the proposal (must survive review and tests):
W=2^40 is only a certificate domain, not a physical coordinate limit. Runtime points outside [-W,W]^2 use the original predicate. Require finite p1 within that domain, finite vector components <=2W, finite normal components <=2, positive finite inv_len_sq and finite projection endpoints. Uncertifiable geometry uses an unbounded enclosure.
For supported points, rounded offsets ox=fl(px-p1x), oy=fl(py-p1y) have magnitude <=2W. Each subtraction has absolute error <= u*2W+eta, where u=2^-53 and eta is the smallest positive subnormal. Every subsequent bound operation rounds outward using next_down/next_up.
For the rounded dot fl(fl(a*ox)+fl(b*oy)), bound multiplication errors by u*|a|*2W+eta and u*|b|*2W+eta, and the final addition error using the sum of the product magnitude/error bounds. Thus the exact real dot lies within E of the computed dot.
If computed perp lies strictly between 0 and 10, the exact normal dot lies in [-En,10+En]. If q=fl(d*inv_len_sq) is between left/right, the exact product lies between next_down(left) and next_up(right). Divide this interval outward by positive inv_len_sq and enlarge by Ev to enclose the exact vector dot.
Invert the exact two-by-two matrix of the stored normal/vector coefficients with outward interval arithmetic. If the determinant interval includes zero, any intermediate is nonfinite, or an interval is invalid, use the unbounded enclosure. The resulting offset intervals contain every accepted rounded offset. Enlarge by the subtraction error and translate by p1, outward, to contain the actual input coordinates.
Source semantics: https://webassembly.github.io/spec/core/exec/numerics.html (ordinary floating operations round to nearest, ties to even); https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html#method.next_up (next_up/next_down, stable since 1.86). The environment remains Rust 1.95.0. No fused/reassociated arithmetic is introduced into the collision predicate.
